papers.title: Finite-Time Singularity Formation for the Three-Dimensional Euler Equations
papers.sentence: Constructs smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time, with the velocity bounded and the vorticity at the origin tending to infinity.

papers.title: Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations
papers.sentence: Proves that there are smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free initial data on ℝ³, and smooth divergence-free data on the torus, whose solutions of the unforced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations blow up in finite time, with the profile obtained from a numerical certificate the authors will release.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted the 15 selected theorems and rejected a control with a deleted hypothesis.

papers.title: Which sums of 1/(2ⁿ − 1) are irrational?
papers.sentence: Proves that the sum of 1/(2ᵃ − 1) over an infinite set A is irrational when A satisfies a weighted summability condition, has a summable divisor cover, or lies in a union of one set of each kind, at every integer base b ≥ 2; Erdős’s question for every infinite A stays open.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted all 51 statements replayed on GitHub Actions.

papers.title: Why the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick order parameter has no gaps
authors: Will Cook, using AI (the three papers)
papers.sentence: A minimising Parisi order parameter of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin glass has no gaps: it increases across every interval in [0, 1), and its derivative is positive between 0 and 1.

papers.title: A nearly quartic separation between randomized and quantum query complexity
papers.sentence: For every power below four there is a total Boolean function whose randomized query complexity exceeds that power of its quantum query complexity, and four is the best possible exponent; Lean checks the optimal exponent with no hypothesis.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted each statement bundle in local runs.

papers.title: Constant-query verification by algebraic encoding
authors: Will Cook, with AI assistance (explanatory reconstruction)
papers.sentence: The PCP theorem: every language in NP has a polynomial-time verifier with logarithmic randomness, constantly many proof-bit queries, perfect completeness and soundness error at most one half, by the algebraic proof of Amireddy, Behera, Srinivasan, Sudan and Willumsgaard.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted the forward theorem, its converse and the equivalence with the reference NP class.

pages.title: Checking a long proof by reading a few bits

papers.title: Contextual Embeddings: Implementing Bound Variables Through Instance Resolution
papers.sentence: Uses instance resolution to define a context-directed isomorphism between a higher-order interface for bound variables and a first-order representation, and proves the round trip in Lean.

papers.title: The SMT-LIB Standard: Version 2.7
papers.sentence: The reference standard for SMT-LIB 2.7, read beside BSmtLib, a Lean formalisation of its lexicon, grammar and parser.

papers.title: The minimum of the coupled spring potential
authors: AI agents under Will Cook’s direction (the page)
papers.sentence: The coupled spring potential U(x₀, x₁) = x₀² + x₀x₁ + x₁² has a local minimum at the origin, proved in PhyslibAlpha by a general second-derivative test.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted the local-minimum theorem and rejected a control that asked for a local maximum.

papers.title: Gauge theory: Physlib’s API map
papers.sentence: Physlib’s own map of its gauge theory formalisation, read beside the Lean files it cites.
